To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) SAR-based optical networks can be used for cluster federation, (2) cluster federation is an effective means to solve large-scale scientific computations, (3) the tradeoff between the user response time and the overall completion time can be controlled by adjusting the level of greed, (4) the locality of the data is a critical factor in determining the overall performance, and (5) the performance of a cluster federation can be improved by carefully controlling the level of greed.

the SAR optical network provides a means of federating geographically distant clusters of computers, and that the performance of federated systems is a function of the degree of locality exploitation, the level of greed, and the degree of user response time control.

SAR optical networks are effective in providing the means for federated clusters to be transparent to the user, that the tradeoff between completion time and user response time can be controlled, and that the performance can be improved by exploiting and giving up localities and controlling the level of greedyness.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and analysis of a novel approach to federating geographically distributed clusters of computers using optical networks.
the design and performance evaluation of a cluster federation architecture that is based on SAR optical networks.
the design and analysis of a new generation of high-performance, large-scale, distributed, and heterogeneous computational systems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the performance of a cluster federation is directly related to the degree of greediness of the system.
SAR optical networks can be effectively used for federating grid clusters to yield a tightly-coupled supercomputer system.
SAR optical networking technologies are very promising and can provide a significant performance improvement in federated cluster computing.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
SAR optical networks are an excellent choice for federating clusters, and that such federations can be effectively controlled to yield systems that are both efficient and responsive to user needs.
the SAR network provides a flexible and cost-effective solution to the problem of federating geographically distant high-performance computational clusters.
the SAR network is capable of providing the necessary performance for the federation of clusters.
The main takeaway from our work is that
SAR optical networks can be used to federate clusters to create systems that are more powerful than the sum of their parts.
the use of optical networks to connect clusters can provide a cost effective solution to the problem of scalability.

federated clusters are an effective way to solve computationally intensive tasks and that the performance of such clusters is dependent on the network topology and on the level of greed in the system.
